# wso2is_remote_logging (Resource)

Sends server logs (audit logs or carbon logs) to a remote HTTP endpoint. This resource only works in the super tenant. When you destroy the resource, the server stops sending the logs. To import, use the log type.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wso2is_remote_logging" "audit" {
  log_type               = "AUDIT"
  remote_url             = "https://logs.example.com/wso2is/audit"
  connect_timeout_millis = "5000"
  username               = "wso2is"
  password               = var.log_password
}

variable "log_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `log_type` (String) `AUDIT` or `CARBON`.
- `remote_url` (String) Endpoint the logs are posted to.

### Optional

- `connect_timeout_millis` (String) Connection timeout in milliseconds.
- `keystore_location` (String) Path, on the server, of a keystore with a client certificate.
- `keystore_password` (String, Sensitive) Keystore password (write-only on the server).
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Basic authentication password (write-only on the server).
- `truststore_location` (String) Path, on the server, of a truststore for the endpoint's certificate.
- `truststore_password` (String, Sensitive) Truststore password (write-only on the server).
- `username` (String) Basic authentication username.
- `verify_hostname` (Boolean) Verify the endpoint's hostname. The default is `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `log_type`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_remote_logging.audit AUDIT
```
